items.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013
items.q: I was playing something for John Surman on a South African group called the Brotherhood of Breath.

ctx.x: What would you have sold? Stuff that you said I don’t need this?

Right. I had two soprano saxophones that I sold. They were a hundred numbers apart. They were both Selmers, and I kick myself for dropping these things. One sounded like an English horn and the other one had a much bigger, more of a jazz soprano sound. So whenever people used to hire me I’d ask them what kind of sound they wanted and bring the appropriate instrument. I sold a really good clarinet. I sold a really good alto flute, a really good bass flute, and I kick myself all over the place for letting go of —…
music, but they were good players. Alan Skidmore was playing tenor on it. A wonderful alto player, an African alto player, named Dudu Pukwana.
